title: What is the Repository Pattern and why is it used?
description: Understand the Repository Pattern for data access abstraction.

data.text: **Question:** What is the Repository Pattern and why is it used?

The Repository Pattern is an abstraction layer between the data source and business logic. It provides a collection-like interface for accessing domain objects, hiding the underlying data access implementation.

**Purpose:**
- Abstracts data access logic from business logic
- Centralizes data access code
- Makes testing easier with mock repositories
- Reduces duplication of query logic

**Key Components:**
- **Repository Interface:** Defines contracts (Get, Add, Update, Delete)
- **Repository Implementation:** Concrete implementation using EF Core, ADO.NET, etc.
- **Unit of Work:** Optional pattern to coordinate multiple repositories

**Benefits:**
- Separation of concerns
- Testability (mock repositories)
- Maintainability
- Flexibility to change data source
